newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertain sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertain sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Friday with the market unclear on the short-term trend, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,480 yuan ($2,588) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at 21,300 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 21,250 and an intra-day high of 21,490.
February rose 40 to 21,140, March gained 20 to 21,240, April fell 20 to 21,390, and June dropped 100 to 21,500.
Combined volume fell to 30,030 tonnes from 34,480.
Copper opened lower but short-covering and fresh buying at low levels pushed prices up for most of the session.
Traders said copper opened lower due to overnight losses on the LME, but many investors did not believe copper would fall sharply enough to trigger large amounts of buying at low levels.
"Although investors were disappointed by copper's poor performance on the LME, they are not pessimistic about the future market trend," one trader said.
"Many investors are willing to buy at the 21,000 yuan level because of the firm spot price," he added. The copper spot price has risen above 21,000 yuan per tonne.
But some traders said copper was not likely to rise sharply in the short term.
"Investors are eager to liquidate their positions at high levels with the approach of the Chinese new year holiday," a second trader said.
Analysts expected copper to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
Aluminium ended with little changed. February held at 14,900, March fell 100 to 15,200, April did not trade, and May was unchanged at 15,600.
Combined volume rose to 560 tonnes from 170.
